name: Suoi Tranh
kicker: Forest stream on the Hàm Ninh range
summary: Forest stream on the Hàm Ninh range: walk in and swim the pools, about 10 km from Dương Đông. Small falls drop over the rocks where the side streams join. The hike is gentle, and the point of it is a dip. You can also camp, fish, and grill beside the water. Go in daylight.
getThere: About 10 km from Dương Đông on the Hàm Ninh road
heroCaption: A fall at Suối Tranh, dropping over dark rocks into the forest pool
body: Walk the forest and swim where the stream pools. Suối Tranh is on the Hàm Ninh range, northeast of the island. From Dương Đông, the Dương Đông–Hàm Ninh road covers about 10 km to the stream. Side streams run through the trees and over rock shelves, then join a main stream that drops in short white falls. You can swim, lie on the flat rocks, camp, fish, and grill the catch. Near the stream, Hang Dơi sits about 200 m up the hill and is about 50 m deep, with stalactites.

The walk to Suối Tranh is a gentle hike, and the point of it is a dip. A harder hike follows the Hàm Ninh mountain trail for an ocean view. Suối Đá Bàn and suối Đá Ngọn are other streams. Đá Ngọn falls in seven tiers. Suối Tranh is the gentle one.

figures.caption: The stream above the fall, running through mossy boulders
figures.alt: Suoi Tranh stream flowing over rocks in the forest on Phu Quoc

gettingThere: From thị trấn Dương Đông, follow the Dương Đông–Hàm Ninh road for about 10 km. The stream is on the northeast side of the island, on the Hàm Ninh range. Hàm Ninh village is 20 km northeast of Dương Đông, so the stream sits on the way toward the village.

legs.heading: From Dương Đông
legs.body: About 10 km along the Dương Đông–Hàm Ninh road. The walk in from there is a gentle hike.

legs.heading: From Hàm Ninh
legs.body: The village is 20 km northeast of Dương Đông, and the stream is about 10 km out on the same road. Pair the swim with the pier and the crab.
